_schema_doc: Single source of truth for the three CUDA `jammi-server` release lanes
(tarball, PyPI wheel, container image): the exact cargo feature list each
lane builds and the capability assertions a real device must prove for
that build. Both the release workflows (`.github/workflows/release-
binaries.yml`, `pypi-server-cuda.yml`, `server-image.yml`) and
`ci/scripts/check_flash_attn_closure.py` / `ci/scripts/
runpod_gpu_prove.sh` read THIS file rather than each carrying their own
copy of the feature list — a fact lives in exactly one place (family T,
DRY). A workflow reads `.lanes.<lane>.cargo_features` with `jq`; the
closure gate reads the whole `lanes` object and asserts, for every lane,
that `capabilities.flash_compiled` matches whether `cargo_features`
actually reaches `jammi-kernels/flash-attn` in the workspace feature
graph; `runpod_gpu_prove.sh` reads a lane's `cargo_features` to build
with EXACTLY that list and derives the `jammi-ai`-applicable subset by
subtracting `server_only_cargo_features` (documented below) — never a
second hardcoded copy of either list.
Adding a lane: add an entry under `lanes`; the closure gate iterates the
object and FAILS on an empty or missing `lanes` key, so a lane can never
silently drop out of PR-time coverage.
Changing what a lane ships: edit `cargo_features` here; the workflow
that builds it and the closure gate that guards it both move in the
same unit (no separate lane-by-lane edit to keep in sync).
`capabilities.fused_op_admission` vs `capabilities.internal_subkernels`:
these are TWO DIFFERENT PROOF MECHANISMS, not one list split by
convenience, and they are the ONLY two a capability block may carry.
Every op named across them appears in EXACTLY ONE — `ci/scripts/
check_release_manifest.py` enforces that, that neither category is
present but EMPTY, that no capability key outside the closed set below
appears at all, and that every lane's `capabilities` block is identical
to every other lane's. The non-category capability keys are exactly
`cuda_compiled`, `flash_compiled` and `flash_dtypes`: build facts about
the lane, naming no op.
`fused_op_admission` is ONLY ops
`crates/jammi-ai/tests/gpu_capability/capability_surface.rs` can attribute
to a real `jammi_kernels::admission::{admit,admit_cascade}` dispatch-
registry key — that test reads THIS key (via `capabilities.
fused_op_admission`) and, for each op it maps, asserts a real
registry-counter DELTA around a live forward + backward + optimizer step
on a real CUDA device — a Fused dispatch that genuinely fired, not a
completed-run inference. Two entries (`softmax`, `rope`) are structurally
UNREACHABLE under `JAMMI_KERNELS_STRICT=1` through ModernBERT's attention
path once `attention_block_fused` admits — see that test's own
`STRICT_UNREACHABLE_OPS` doc — so the test logs them informationally
rather than asserting `Holds`; they stay listed here (removing them would
misrepresent them as never covered by fused-kernel authoring, which is
false — they DO have real registry keys, just not an independently
provable Strict-mode run through this attention path) but a manifest
consumer must not read every `fused_op_admission` entry as "asserted
Holds" without also reading that test's own per-op caveats.
An op is named here by its DTYPE-NEUTRAL name even when the registry keys
it actually dispatches under are dtype-keyed: `cast_scale` admits under
`cast_scale_bf16_f32`/`cast_scale_f16_f32` and `cast_add` under
`cast_add_bf16`/`cast_add_f16`, both through `admit_cast_boundary` in
`crates/jammi-kernels/src/ops/low_rank_residual_linear.rs` (called from
that op's BF16 and F16 backward arms). The report-name -> registry-key
mapping is a static table in `jammi-kernels` (`PROBED_OPS`), and
`capability_surface.rs` asserts set-equality between THIS file's
categories and that table by kind, so a name here that no table row maps
fails loudly instead of going silently unprobed. `adamw_step` is the
optimizer-step member of this category: it admits under
`adamw_step_fused` (`crates/jammi-ai/src/fine_tune/adamw.rs`'s `admit`
call), F32 ONLY — proven by the `capability_surface` probe's own real
optimizer step, which is exactly why that probe runs backward + one AdamW
step rather than a forward alone.
`internal_subkernels` is the DIFFERENT mechanism: an op with real CUDA
kernels and dispatch arms that is launched DIRECTLY by an admitted PARENT
op and has no `admit()`/`admit_cascade()` call of its own —
`rope_positions` (launched bare as `crate::cuda::rope_positions::cuda_fwd`
from the flash-attention op) and `scaled_cast_add` (constructed bare as
`ScaledCastAdd::new` in `low_rank_residual_linear`'s epilogue). Each entry
names its `parent` and its `launch_site` — by FILE, never a line number,
so the citation does not rot on an unrelated edit. Such an op is proven by
(1) compiling in this lane's build and (2) its PARENT's admitted dispatch
being OBSERVED: a registry delta on the parent's key under
`JAMMI_KERNELS_STRICT=1` in the `capability_surface` probe. The parent
cannot have dispatched Fused without running the sub-kernel it launches
unconditionally. NEVER by a counter of its own — there is none. A
consumer must therefore read an entry here as neither "unreachable" NOR
"independently admitted": it is reached exactly when its parent is, and
carries no admission decision of its own to report. `parent` names the
identity whose observed delta IS the proof: `attention_block_flash` is the
flash cascade's registry key (this file's own `flash_compiled`/
`flash_dtypes` describe that lane), and `low_rank_residual_linear` is a
`fused_op_admission` op above (registry key `lora_linear_fused`).
THERE IS NO COMPILED-ONLY CATEGORY. A kernel with no `admit()`/
`admit_cascade()` call site AND no admitted parent that launches it has NO
category here at all: the only thing a shipped build could say about it is
"it compiled", which is not a capability a consumer can act on, and a
category holding exactly that is an empty proof slot the next unwired
kernel gets filed into instead of being decided. Such a kernel is either
WIRED — given a real dispatch site, which lands it in
`fused_op_admission` — or DELETED, in the same unit as its authoring. The
decision is a measurement against a threshold fixed BEFORE the numbers are
seen, not a judgement call at review time; see `crates/jammi-kernels/
artifacts/cuda-runs/2026-09-01-axpy-census-bdeb80c-a100-pcie.json` for the
precedent, where a pre-registered rule (wire iff the op's share reaches 2%
of per-step GPU time on some shipped leg AND one dispatch site covers at
least half of that share) measured 0.007% / 0.026% / 0.027% across the
three shipped dtype legs and the kernel was deleted rather than kept as a
compiled-only row.
Promotion is always a code edit and a manifest edit in ONE unit: wiring a
real `admit()`/`admit_cascade()` call site (and its `PROBED_OPS` row)
promotes an op into `fused_op_admission`; giving it an admitted parent
that launches it directly moves it into `internal_subkernels`. Never a
manifest-only move.

cu12-tarball._doc: The self-contained CUDA `jammi-server` tarball (binary + bundled CUDA runtime .so's + LD_LIBRARY_PATH launcher).

cu12-wheel._doc: The `jammi-server-cu12` PyPI wheel, built through `_pypi-server.yml` (reusable) by `.github/workflows/pypi-server-cuda.yml`.

cu12-image._doc: The `jammi-ai-server-cu12` container image's `runtime-cuda`/`builder-cuda` Dockerfile stage, published by `.github/workflows/server-image.yml`.

_doc: Proof surface == shipped surface (esc-081): the DECLARED set of
`(crate, kind)` pairs `ci/scripts/runpod_gpu_prove.sh` must invoke on a
real device. `kind` is one of `release` (a `cargo build --release`/
`cargo run --release` invocation), `test` (a `cargo test` invocation
carrying a `--features` tuple, with or without `--no-run`), or
`default` (a `cargo test` invocation with NO `--features` flag at all
-- canonicalizes to an empty feature list). `ci/scripts/
prove_surface.py` computes, for a declared pair, `expected(crate,
kind) = (this file's own `lanes.cu12-tarball.cargo_features` ∩
crate's OWN `[features]` table keys) ∪ (this entry's `prove_only`,
iff kind == test)` -- read hermetically via stdlib `tomllib`, never a
second hardcoded copy of a crate's feature list. `check_flash_attn_
closure.py` asserts SET EQUALITY between THIS declared pair set and
the script's own invocations (one literal tuple text per pair,
preceded by a `PROVE_TUPLE` echo) -- a dropped `--features`, a
deleted proof invocation, or an unlisted pair each FAIL. `prove_only`
names a feature the shipped lane does not itself require but the
PROOF needs to actually exercise the gated suite (`live-gpu-tests`
gates every real-device `#[test]` in this workspace) -- it is added
only to a `test`-kind pair, never to `release` (a release build ships
exactly the lane's own features, nothing test-only).
Features that exist on `jammi-server` with no `jammi-ai` equivalent
(broker/cloud-storage plumbing the embedded engine crate does not
carry). A consumer deriving the `jammi-ai`-applicable subset of a
lane's `cargo_features` (e.g. `runpod_gpu_prove.sh`'s capability-
surface build, which runs `cargo test -p jammi-ai --features <subset>`
rather than `-p jammi-server`) subtracts this list from
`lanes.<lane>.cargo_features`. Every lane above resolves to
`["cuda", "flash-attn"]` on `jammi-ai` once these are removed.
